outro.line: Save this before you email your waitlist

hook.title: *300* signups and I never checked who can *read* them

beats.text: My waitlist has 300 signups. I never checked who can read them.
Nobody looking isn't the same as nobody able to look.
Who can read that table right now?
Me. And the app.
Open a private window. You can read all 300.
beats.say: Open a private window. You can read all three hundred.

beats.text: Okay. Like two people. Tops.
Anyone with the link. Not two.
Step one. Type /security-review.
beats.say: Step one. Type slash security review.

panel.title: Run the security check
panel.html:
~/waitlist-app $ claude
> /security-review
Scanning 38 files...
HIGH signups table: readable by anyone

beats.text: Wait. It says readable by anyone?
Anyone. Including the bots.
Step two. Ask it to flag what it's unsure of.

panel.title: Flag what it's unsure of
panel.html:
Which of these are safe to leave public?
I'm not sure about the email column. Flagged.
email: unsurenames: fine

beats.text: I'd have just said it's fine.
That's the whole point of flagging.
Step three. Plan first, then touch the rules.

panel.title: Plan before the rules
panel.html:
Plan: no edits yet
1. Only the owner reads signups
2. Public form can add, not read
you: just change the rules
last time: signups stopped for two days

beats.text: Just change the rules. I know what I'm doing.
Last time you said that, signups stopped for two days.
Okay. Show me the plan.
Step four. Test it as a stranger.

panel.title: Test it as a stranger
panel.html:
Read the signups table.
Access denied: signups
owner only

beats.text: Denied. Good. That's the answer I want.
Two minutes. Better than two days.
So I'm basically a security expert now.
You're a waitlist with a lock on it. Congratulations.
